qa_pairs.question: Assuming that the 'User feedback on their own sleep quality' and the 'Factors Affecting Sleep' are independent conditions, is it true that the group with the highest combined probability, 'Users reporting occasional sleep problems + Can't resist using mobile phones/tablets before sleep', has the largest proportion?
qa_pairs.explanation: In chart_100_1, the proportion of 'Occasional sleep problems' is the highest (47.0%). In chart_100_4, 'Can't resist using mobile phones/tablets before sleep' is the top factor affecting sleep (15.9%). The combination of these two may form the largest intersection.

qa_pairs.question: The 'Sleep Scores of Different Generations' shows that the Post - 60s+ has the highest score (83.5). Does it mean that this group is less troubled by the 'Top 10 Factors Affecting Sleep'?
qa_pairs.explanation: A higher score usually indicates better sleep quality. The 'Top 10 Factors Affecting Sleep' such as using mobile phones before sleep and staying up late are more common among younger groups. Therefore, the Post - 60s+ may have relatively fewer interference factors.

qa_pairs.question: Both the 'User - reported sleep problems (TOP10)' and the 'Top 10 Factors Affecting Sleep' mention issues related to'staying up late'. Can we infer that'staying up late' is an important cause of sleep disorders?
qa_pairs.explanation: In the sleep problems, 'Habitually staying up late' accounts for 10.6%. In the factors affecting sleep, the sum of 'Habituated to staying up late without motivation to change' and 'Staying up late to study or work affects rest' reaches 23.1%. It can be seen that'staying up late' is a pain point frequently reported by users, and it can be inferred as one of the main causes.

qa_pairs.question: Please calculate the ratio of the proportion of users who reported 'No problems, slept very well' to the proportion of users who reported 'Too short deep sleep time'. Round the result to 2 decimal places. Answer: xx.xx times
qa_pairs.explanation: The proportion of users who reported 'No problems, slept very well' is 18.7%. The proportion of users who reported 'Too short deep sleep time' is 13.8%. 18.7% ÷ 13.8% ≈ 1.355. Rounding to 2 decimal places gives 1.36 times.

qa_pairs.question: Please calculate the ratio of the proportion of users who reported 'Habitually staying up late' to the proportion of the factor 'Habituated to staying up late without motivation to change' that affects sleep. Round the result to 2 decimal places. Answer: xx.xx times
qa_pairs.explanation: The proportion of users who reported 'Habitually staying up late' is 10.6%. The proportion of the factor 'Habituated to staying up late without motivation to change' that affects sleep is 13.6%. 10.6% ÷ 13.6% ≈ 0.779. Rounding to 2 decimal places gives 0.78 times.

qa_pairs.question: Please multiply the sleep score of the Post - 60s+ group by the proportion of users who reported 'Yes, have relatively serious sleep problems'. What is the approximate result (rounded to 1 decimal place)? Answer: xx.x points
qa_pairs.explanation: The sleep score of the Post - 60s+ group is 83.5. The proportion of users who reported 'Yes, have relatively serious sleep problems' is 8.7%. 83.5 × 8.7% ≈ 7.2645. Rounding to 1 decimal place gives 7.3 points.
